items.title: Nigeria's president launches re-election manifesto but can he regain voters' trust?
items.summary: President Tinubu faces re-election with cost of living and economic hardship being the major issues for many voters Nigeria's President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has launched his re-election manifesto, promising to grow the economy, tackle insecurity and address housing shortages The plan targets 6% annual economic growth by 2031, 78,000 additional security personnel and 200,000 affordable homes Titled From Reform to Prosperity, the manifesto builds on Tinubu's first-term economic reforms, including the removal of the fuel subsidy, which has pushed up living costs Nigeria is due to hold a general election in January 2027, with Peter Obi and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar among Tinubu's main challengers The manifesto, launched on 10 November by his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), reflects the government's bid to win back the trust of Nigerians Elected in 2023, Tinubu undertook a series of economic reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidies, the harmonisation of official and parallel foreign exchange rates, and tax reforms in Africa's largest oil producer "That…

items.title: Driven by LNG megaprojects, FDI reaches 1.88 billion dollars
items.summary: Maputo, 11 Nov (AIM) – The Bank of Mozambique, in its role as regulator of the national financial system, has recorded, in the first half of 2026, 1.88 billion US dollars as a result of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in the country. This figure corresponds to 33 percent of the amount attracted throughout 2025, mainly in the gas and mining sectors. According to data from Bank of Mozambique, this amount consists of inflows of 1.286 billion dollars in the first quarter of 2026 and 594.5 million dollars in the second quarter. The document points out that despite the slowdown observed between April and June, the structure of foreign investment remains largely dominated by megaprojects associated with natural resources, particularly natural gas, oil and mining, which continue to absorb most of the external capital directed towards the Mozambican economy.

items.title: African writing award probe finds 'no evidence' winning story was AI generated
items.summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza, who lives in Harare, says he was inspired by a poem about fish tanks to write a story about his family struggles The Caine Prize for African Writing has said that after an internal review it has found no evidence that Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza had used generative AI to write his winning short story and confirmed him as the winner of this year's £10,000 ($13,000) award Ellah Wakatama, chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees, said the matter had been investigated following an article in US magazine The Atlantic with the headline, Yet Another Literary Prizewinner Seems to Be AI "From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human written," she said in a video posted on X The accusation had caused a social media uproar and Kundizeza had denied the allegation The Atlantic article by journalist Vauhini Vara alleged that AI-detection software Pangram had shown his work about a boy whose family falls on hard times was entirely AI generated Her allegations followed rows over other literary prizes this year, in…

items.title: VW scraps production modernization plan citing tough financial straits
items.summary: VW has announced that it will scrap large-scale modernization in light of its current economic situation. Employee representatives accuse leadership of putting short-term profits before long-term company viability Volkswagen, Europe's largest automaker , cited financial constraints on Wednesday when announcing that it will not carry out modernization plans as previously outlined in its project "Gamechanger" scheme A VW spokesman said all investments at the company are currently under review and that a planned large-scale casting facility at its main Wolfsburg site would not be moving forward despite years of preparation, investment and the stated goal of future-proofing the company for a rapidly evolving production landscape In his statement, the spokesman said the scrapping of Gamechanger did not mean the company would forego development of its Scalable Systems Platform (SSP) program, which aims to create a shared electric platform for future VW models like the ID.

items.title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
items.summary: On Thursday Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Moscow and Dublin to hold talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." "I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of citizens have hit the streets to protest Spain's housing crisis after millions of union workers staged a general strike. Housing.
